another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant does not live in the UK
  - Child is 13 (under 16)
  - Claimant contributes £26.05/week towards child's upkeep (>= £26.05) and no other claimaint has priority

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to ask you about your child:

**How old is your child?** 

The eligibility rules depend on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Generally eligible (with some conditions)
- **16-19**: May be eligible if in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have more than one child you're inquiring about, please let me know about all of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - Alex, who's 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So you have one child, Alex, who is 13 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, that's a good start. Now I need to check a few more things.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

This is important because children working 24 or more hours per week and not in approved education/training are not eligible for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 13, so they're still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is 13 and in school, they're not working at all. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking if Alex is receiving benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in their own name (not as part of your household claim, but in their own right).

For a 13-year-old, this would be unusual, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Let me continue checking the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 13 and in school, they're almost certainly not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this as certain types of apprenticeships can affect eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - they're just in regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, let me move on to the next part of the assessment, which focuses on you as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. **Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if **ANY** of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources and not claiming certain benefits
6. You have pre-settled status and are a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Do any of these apply to you?** Most people will simply normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since you're living abroad, let me check if you might still qualify under special circumstances.

**Are you living abroad as a Crown servant** (such as diplomatic staff, armed forces personnel, or other UK government employees working overseas)? 

Or are you living in one of the certain qualifying countries where UK Child Benefit can still be claimed?

These special circumstances allow people living outside the UK to still claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that - I'm just living abroad for personal reasons.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Unfortunately, this means you don't meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment - Result

I'm sorry, but **you are not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

### Why you're not eligible:

While Alex meets all the child-related requirements:
- ✓ Age 13 (under 16)
- ✓ Not working full-time
- ✓ Not receiving benefits in their own right
- ✓ Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**The issue is with the residency requirement:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements because you are living abroad for personal reasons and are not a Crown servant or living in one of the qualifying countries.

### What this means:

To claim Child Benefit, you must either:
- **Normally live in the UK**, or
- Have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with additional conditions), or
- Be a Crown servant living abroad, or
- Be living in certain qualifying countries

### What you can do:

- If you **return to live in the UK**, you would then meet the residency requirements and could claim Child Benefit for Alex
- If your circumstances change (for example, if you become a Crown servant), you may become eligible

If you have any questions or if your situation changes, you can find more information at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

reasonings: Alex is 13 years old and meets the child-related criteria (under 16, not working full-time, not receiving benefits in their own right, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship). However, the claimant does not meet the UK residency requirements. The claimant is living abroad for personal reasons and is not a Crown servant or living in qualifying countries. Therefore, the claim for Alex is ineligible due to the claimant's failure to meet residency requirements.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant has one child, Alex (age 13), who meets all child-specific eligibility criteria. However, the claimant is living abroad for personal reasons and does not meet any of the UK residency requirements necessary to claim Child Benefit. As a result, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
